source: Had you stepped on board the Pequod at a certain juncture of this post-mortemizing of the whale; and had you strolled forward nigh the windlass, pretty sure am I that you would have scanned with no small curiosity a very strange, enigmatical object, which you would have seen there, lying along lengthwise in the lee scuppers. Not the wondrous cistern in the whale’s huge head; not the prodigy of his unhinged lower jaw; not the miracle of his symmetrical tail; none of these would so surprise you, as half a glimpse of that unaccountable cone,—longer than a Kentuckian is tall, nigh a foot in diameter at the base, and jet-black as Yojo, the ebony idol of Queequeg. And an idol, indeed, it is; or, rather, in old times, its likeness was. Such an idol as that found in the secret groves of Queen Maachah in Judea; and for worshipping which, King Asa, her son, did depose her, and destroyed the idol, and burnt it for an abomination at the brook Kedron, as darkly set forth in the 15th chapter of the First Book of Kings.

Look at the sailor, called the mincer, who now comes along, and assisted by two allies, heavily backs the grandissimus, as the mariners call it, and with bowed shoulders, staggers off with it as if he were a grenadier carrying a dead comrade from the field. Extending it upon the forecastle deck, he now proceeds cylindrically to remove its dark pelt, as an African hunter the pelt of a boa. This done he turns the pelt inside out, like a pantaloon leg; gives it a good stretching, so as almost to double its diameter; and at last hangs it, well spread, in the rigging, to dry. Ere long, it is taken down; when removing some three feet of it, towards the pointed extremity, and then cutting two slits for arm-holes at the other end, he lengthwise slips himself bodily into it. The mincer now stands before you invested in the full canonicals of his calling. Immemorial to all his order, this investiture alone will adequately protect him, while employed in the peculiar functions of his office.

That office consists in mincing the horse-pieces of blubber for the pots; an operation which is conducted at a curious wooden horse, planted endwise against the bulwarks, and with a capacious tub beneath it, into which the minced pieces drop, fast as the sheets from a rapt orator’s desk. Arrayed in decent black; occupying a conspicuous pulpit; intent on bible leaves; what a candidate for an archbishopric, what a lad for a Pope were this mincer!*

*Bible leaves! Bible leaves! This is the invariable cry from the mates to the mincer. It enjoins him to be careful, and cut his work into as thin slices as possible, inasmuch as by so doing the business of boiling out the oil is much accelerated, and its quantity considerably increased, besides perhaps improving it in quality.

modern_en.title: Chapter 95 — The Cassock
paragraphs: Had you stepped aboard the Pequod at a certain point in this post-mortem of the whale and strolled forward near the windlass, I am quite sure you would have studied with no small curiosity a very strange, puzzling object lying lengthwise in the lee scuppers. Not the wondrous cistern in the whale's huge head; not the wonder of his unhinged lower jaw; not the miracle of his symmetrical tail — none of these would so surprise you as half a glimpse of that unaccountable cone, longer than a Kentuckian is tall, nearly a foot in diameter at the base, and jet-black as Yojo, the ebony idol of Queequeg. And an idol, indeed, it is — or rather, in old times, its likeness was. Such an idol as that found in the secret groves of Queen Maachah in Judea, and for worshipping which King Asa, her son, deposed her, destroyed the idol, and burnt it as an abomination at the brook Kedron, as darkly set forth in the fifteenth chapter of the First Book of Kings.

Look at the sailor called the mincer, who now comes along and, assisted by two helpers, heavily shoulders the grandissimus, as the mariners call it, and with bowed shoulders staggers off with it as if he were a grenadier carrying a dead comrade from the field. Laying it upon the forecastle deck, he proceeds to remove its dark skin cylindrically, as an African hunter skins a boa. This done, he turns the skin inside out like a trouser leg, gives it a good stretching so as almost to double its diameter, and at last hangs it, well spread, in the rigging to dry. Before long it is taken down. Removing some three feet from the pointed end and then cutting two slits for armholes at the other end, he lengthwise slips himself bodily into it. The mincer now stands before you invested in the full canonicals (the clerical vestments) of his calling. As it has for all his order from time immemorial, this investiture alone will adequately protect him while employed in the peculiar functions of his office.

That office consists in mincing the horse-pieces of blubber for the pots — an operation conducted at a curious wooden horse planted endwise against the bulwarks, with a capacious tub beneath it into which the minced pieces drop, fast as the sheets from a rapt orator's desk. Arrayed in decent black, occupying a conspicuous pulpit, intent on Bible leaves — what a candidate for an archbishopric, what a lad for a Pope, this mincer!*

*Bible leaves! Bible leaves! This is the invariable cry from the mates to the mincer. It commands him to be careful and cut his work into the thinnest possible slices, inasmuch as by doing so the business of boiling out the oil is much accelerated and its quantity considerably increased, besides perhaps improving it in quality.

modern_da.title: Kapitel 95 — Kasen
paragraphs: Hvis du var gået om bord på Pequod på et bestemt tidspunkt i denne hvalens obduktion og havde gået forover i nærheden af ankerspillet, er jeg ganske sikker på, at du med ikke ringe nysgerrighed ville have studeret en meget mærkelig, gådefuld genstand, der lå på langs i læ-speigatterne. Ikke den vidunderlige cisterne i hvalens enorme hoved, ikke underet ved hans udleddede underkæbe, ikke miraklet i hans symmetriske hale — ingen af dem ville overraske dig så meget som et halvt glimt af den uforklarlige kegle, længere end en mand fra Kentucky er høj, næsten en fod i diameter ved roden og kulsort som Yojo, Queequegs ibenholtsidol. Og et idol er det i sandhed — eller rettere, i gamle dage var dets lignelse det. Et idol som det, der blev fundet i dronning Maachas hemmelige lunde i Judæa, og for at have dyrket det afsatte kong Asa, hendes søn, hende, ødelagde idolet og brændte det som en vederstyggelighed ved bækken Kedron, som det mørkt er fortalt i femtende kapitel af Første Kongebog.

Se på matrosen, der kaldes hakkeren, som nu kommer forbi og, hjulpet af to hjælpere, tungt tager grandissimus, som sømændene kalder den, på skulderen, og med bøjede skuldre vakler af sted med den, som var han en grenader, der bærer en død kammerat fra marken. Han lægger den på bakkedækket og begynder at tage dens mørke hud af i ét stykke rundt om, som en afrikansk jæger flår en boaslange. Når det er gjort, vender han skindet med vrangen ud som et bukseben, giver det en ordentlig udstrækning, så det næsten fordobles i diameter, og hænger det til sidst, godt udspilet, op i rigningen for at tørre. Lidt efter tages det ned. Han skærer omkring tre fod af i den spidse ende og laver to slidser til armhuler i den anden ende, og så smutter han på langs helt ind i det. Hakkeren står nu foran dig iklædt de fulde kanoniske klæder (præstedragten) for sit kald. Som det har været for hele hans stand fra tidernes morgen, vil denne iklædning alene beskytte ham tilstrækkeligt, mens han udfører sit embedes ejendommelige gerning.

Det embede består i at hakke spækstykkerne til gryderne — en handling, der foregår ved en mærkelig træhest, sat på højkant mod essingen, med en rummelig balje under, som de hakkede stykker falder ned i, hurtigt som arkene fra en henrykt talers pult. Klædt i anstændigt sort, på en iøjnefaldende prædikestol, optaget af bibelblade — sikken en kandidat til et ærkebispedømme, sikken en dreng til pave, denne hakker!*

*Bibelblade! Bibelblade! Det er det altid gentagne råb fra styrmændene til hakkeren. Det befaler ham at passe på og skære sit arbejde i de tyndest mulige skiver, eftersom det gør arbejdet med at koge olien ud meget hurtigere og øger mængden betydeligt, foruden at det måske også forbedrer kvaliteten.
